prompt:
Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with concussion after a low-speed head-on collision. The patient had 16 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1197; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Some exam findings support the injury; other tests are normal.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
text: The patient presented following a low-speed head-on collision with symptoms consistent with concussion, including headache, dizziness, and difficulty concentrating. The mechanism of injury and the force involved are well matched to the reported symptoms. Over the course of 16 visits, care followed a typical progression: early focus on symptom monitoring, cognitive and vestibular rest, and gradual reintroduction of activity, with visit frequency tapering as the patient improved. Examination findings were mixed. Some findings, including vestibular and balance abnormalities, support the diagnosis of concussion, while other neurological and imaging-related assessments returned normal results. No prior injury to the same body region is documented in the available history. Billing records reflect single, appropriate charges for each service with no duplicated or repeated billing. Current status is improving, and the patient is expected to return to baseline function with continued self-management and follow-up as needed.
